subject: Implementing social relations models in Stan

messages.author: c481bd0447c0caf2
messages.subject: Implementing social relations models in Stan
parts:
Hi,

I've been trying to implement a social relations model in Stan, using the BUGS model published by Koster and Leckie (2014) for inspiration (a copy of their BUGS model code is available here). I'm new to Stan and mainly wanted to check I've gone about implementing the SRM in the right way (especially calculating the deviance and/or log likelihood in this bivariate response version of the model). I imagine that there's a lot to be done to optimise this so any tips would be greatly appreciated too. The model code is:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;           # no. dyads
  int<lower=0> N_hh;        # no. households
  int<lower=1> hidA[N];     # household A in each dyad
  int<lower=1> hidB[N];     # household B in each dyad
  int<lower=0> giftsAB[N];  # no. gifts given from household A to B
  int<lower=0> giftsBA[N];  # no. gifts given from household B to A
}
transformed data {
  vector[2] zero_vector;
  zero_vector = rep_vector(0, 2);
}
parameters {
  real alpha;                 # intercept
  
  vector[2] gr[N_hh];         # per-individual random effect
  corr_matrix[2] R_gr;        # giver-receiver covariance matrix - prior correlation
  vector<lower=0>[2] tau_gr;  # giver-receiver covariance matrix - prior scale
  
  vector[2] dd[N];            # dyadic effect
  corr_matrix[2] R_dd;        # dyadic covariance matrix - prior correlation
  vector<lower=0>[2] tau_dd;  # dyadic covariance matrix - prior scale
}
transformed parameters {
  cov_matrix[2] COV_gr;       # giver-receiver covariance matrix
  cov_matrix[2] COV_dd;       # dyadic covariance matrix
  
  COV_gr = quad_form_diag(R_gr, tau_gr);
  COV_dd = quad_form_diag(R_dd, tau_dd);
}
model {
  vector[N] lambdaAB;
  vector[N] lambdaBA;

  # prior for giver and receiver bivariate normal random effects
  # instead of a scaled inverse Wishart as the prior on the giver-receiver covariance matrix, use the approach described on p.144 of the Stan manual
  R_gr ~ lkj_corr( 2 );
  tau_gr ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
  gr ~ multi_normal( zero_vector , COV_gr );
  
  # dyadic random effects
  R_dd ~ lkj_corr( 2 );
  tau_dd ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
  dd ~ multi_normal( zero_vector, COV_dd );
  
  alpha ~ normal(0, 10);  # prior for intercept
  
  for(i in 1:N) {
    lambdaAB[i] = alpha + gr[hidA[i], 1] + gr[hidB[i], 2] + dd[i, 1];
    lambdaBA[i] = alpha + gr[hidB[i], 1] + gr[hidA[i], 2] + dd[i, 2];
  }
  
  giftsAB ~ poisson_log( lambdaAB );
  giftsBA ~ poisson_log( lambdaBA );
}
generated quantities{
  vector[N] lambdaAB;
  vector[N] lambdaBA;
  real dev = 0;
  for ( i in 1:N ) {
    lambdaAB[i] = alpha + gr[hidA[i], 1] + gr[hidB[i], 2] + dd[i, 1];
    lambdaBA[i] = alpha + gr[hidB[i], 2] + gr[hidA[i], 2] + dd[i, 2];
  }
  dev = dev + (-2)*( poisson_log_lpmf( giftsAB | lambdaAB ) + poisson_log_lpmf( giftsBA | lambdaBA ) );
}

I'd also like to make a version of this that fits only a single response variable to long-format data, but I'm a bit confused about how to calculate the dyad effects ('dd') in this case. What I've changed so far is:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;                             # No. observations
  int<lower=1> N_dyads;                       # No. dyads
  int<lower=1> Dyad_id[N];                    # Dyad ID for each observation
  //... rest same as above
}
model {
  vector[N] lambda;
  //... same as above
  for(i in 1:N) {
    lambda[i] = alpha + gr[hidA[i], 1] + gr[hidB[i], 2] + dd[Dyad_id[i], 1] + dd[Dyad_id[i], 2];
  }
  gifts ~ poisson_log( lambda );
}


Thanks in advance for your help!

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Implementing social relations models in Stan
parts:
That looks OK. I don't have time to do fine-grained checking,
but you can compare results to BUGS and I'd also suggest simulating
data from the model to make sure you can recover parameters.

For efficiency:

1. Use Cholesky factors of correlation matrices---there's an example
of how to scale these in the regression chapter of the manual. In the
2 x 2 case it's probably not a big deal. The prior eta = 2 in the
LKJ isn't very strong.

2. Vectorize this:

for(i in 1:N) {
lambdaAB[i] = alpha + gr[hidA[i], 1] + gr[hidB[i], 2] + dd[i, 1];
lambdaBA[i] = alpha + gr[hidB[i], 1] + gr[hidA[i], 2] + dd[i, 2];
}

as

lambdaAB = alpha = gr[hidA, 1] + gr[hidB, 2] + dd[, 1];

and similarly for lambdaBA.

3. Unless you need to save the transformed covar matrices, just
define them as local variables in the model block. We now have
compound declare and define, so that's as easy as putting

cov_matrix[2] COV_dd = quad_form_diag(R_dd, tau_dd);

in the first line of the model block. But you should really do (1)
first, as it'll look a bit different (don't need quad form as you're
working in matrix "square roots" with Cholesky factors).

4. The deviance calculation are tricky when there are latent parameter.
Those really need to be marginalized out to get your likelihoods. And
we don't generally recommend computing things like DIC, which is what
they're usually used for. See the discussion in Vehtari, Gelman and
Gabry's papers or in Gelman et al.'s BDA book.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Implementing social relations models in Stan
parts:
Thanks very much, Bob. Your suggestions have sped it up considerably.

Regarding your point (4), I'd prefer to calculate WAIC rather than DIC, so I changed the generated quantities section to this:

generated quantities{
  vector[N] log_lik;
  
  for (i in 1:N) {
    log_lik[i] = poisson_log_lpmf( giftsAB[i] | alpha + gr[hidA[i], 1] + gr[hidB[i], 2] + dd[i, 1] ) + 
                 poisson_log_lpmf( giftsBA[i] | alpha + gr[hidB[i], 1] + gr[hidA[i], 2] + dd[i, 2] );
  }
}

- Matt
